headline: The Wallet That Knew Before the Market
lede: Four Polygon transactions assembled a remarkably well-timed position in a Jensen Huang prediction market. The blockchain preserves the timing and profit, but not the trader’s identity—or proof that the information was illicit.

headline: Linux Finds a New Home in the Browser
lede: Trynix runs more than 300,000 Nix packages through WebAssembly, turning the browser into a surprisingly capable Linux playground. Firefox and OpenGL demos work; the nested Firefox experiment takes more patience than most users possess.

headline: Ladybird Opens Its First Alpha
lede: A new browser engine arrives without Chromium or Firefox under the hood. Ladybird’s macOS and Linux alpha is crash-prone and incomplete, but ready for developers, testers, and the web’s less forgiving edge cases.

headline: Replay Turns Waiting Into a Performance Bug
lede: Rewind’s new command reconstructs a program’s critical path from deterministic virtual-machine recordings. Instead of guessing what to trace during a slow run, engineers can inspect the delays afterward—and replay them.
pullquote: The slow path is often a waiting path.

headline: Stalwart Makes Exchange Migration Plausible
lede: Stalwart 1.2.0 adds MAPI, EWS, ActiveSync, and Autodiscover compatibility, allowing familiar clients to connect to an open-source mail stack. It is a transition layer for organizations leaving Exchange—not a promise to reproduce every Microsoft feature.

headline: EPYC’s Decade Produces a 12.1× Leap
lede: A dual-socket 2017 EPYC system meets AMD’s modern Venice processors in a workload-based comparison. The geometric mean lands at 12.1×, with core counts, memory bandwidth, architecture, and power efficiency all contributing to the distance.

headline: Nvidia Brings Jensen Huang Back
lede: Nvidia’s board has reinstated its co-founder after allegations involving workplace conduct and a possible intelligence connection. Shares jumped, while an investigation into company secrets and export controls continues.

headline: Drones Turn Salvage Yards Into Maps
lede: Aerial photography gives Illinois salvage yards an overhead index: towing lots, recyclers, rows of vehicles, and the parts hidden between them. The project is simple in apparatus and practical in aim—less wandering, more finding.

headline: Debian Rebuilds Its Bandwidth Toolkit
lede: Debian splits iperf clients and servers into cleaner packages, adds templated systemd services, and introduces fireperf for parallel and bidirectional testing. The old package names remain as a compatibility bridge while the network bench gets modern plumbing.

headline: Arctic Makes Concurrent Trees Less Compromised
lede: Arctic is a lock-free adaptive radix tree designed to support updates alongside range and prefix scans. Its freezing protocol and memory-reclamation scheme improve throughput in RocksDB and Turso, though its scans are not linearizable.
